column6: Promise: 'Know every deal. Coach every rep. Forget nothing.'; one memory in three layers. Layer 1 ('What was said') is backed by Built call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library); its email and Slack sources are In build / Planned. In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'. Flagged by the Narrative: 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)'.
column7: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): The shared-memory whitespace narrows further in this batch. Showpad's homepage states it 'holds what no other system has: the content, coaching signals, and deal-stage context' — the closest direct claim to PitchSense's one-shared-memory frame among the ten homepages inspected across batches 1-3. Salesloft's 'Signals' concept and Mindtickle's 'decade of rep behavior data... compounding' are adjacent but framed as signal-capture and behavior-data assets rather than a single connected memory. Testing question: can PitchSense's 'one memory connecting four intelligences' be differentiated from Showpad's foundation claim by depth of connection (calls+CRM+emails+Slack+documents in one memory) rather than by existence of a foundation? Showpad's claim is a vendor statement, not verified architecture. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Differentiating by depth of connection (calls+CRM+emails+Slack+documents in one memory) is not available today: CRM, email and Slack are In build or Planned. Built depth is calls + documents + practice.

column6: Built: AI voice roleplays (11 scenario types, 3 languages, micro roleplays); tracks; skills and scoring set by Enablement; scores with evidence on every practice session; readiness per rep and scenario; coaching suggestions for managers; one-click drills with before-and-after results. In build: pre-call drill tied to a specific upcoming call. Planned: scoring real calls on your skills. Flagged: 'Checks the score on the next real call'.
column7: INTERPRETATION: Coaching and roleplay are prominently claimed by three of the four inspected vendors — a material change from batches 1-2 where AI roleplay was unfeatured on homepages. Mindtickle promotes 'Try AI Role Play' as a hero CTA (to a dedicated roleplay product site, roleplay.mindtickle.com) and cites Cisco's roleplay results (31% deal size); Allego has AI Role Play & Coaching as a top-level nav product; Showpad features Roleplay AI as a Genie product. Salesloft's inspected pages showed no roleplay proposition (page-scoped observation). PitchSense's 'AI roleplay as additional differentiation' hypothesis is weakened against the three inspected enablement vendors that prominently promote it (Mindtickle, Allego, Showpad — not Salesloft) — roleplay is prominently featured messaging among these inspected vendors (Phase 1 roleplay specialists should be checked before generalizing beyond these vendors). Testing question: what remains distinctive about PitchSense's roleplay (memory-grounded scenarios from real deals?) vs. these established offerings? NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Scenarios from your own documents are Built ('Practice built from your own documents'); a pre-call drill tied to a specific call is In build; 'memory-grounded scenarios from real deals' needs Planned real-call scoring.
